title: Career roadmap · Data Policy Advisor
summary: Build from data science and computational social science into evidence-based data governance, privacy, AI regulation, digital policy and responsible data use.

facts.Timeline assumption: The roadmap assumes a 2026-start Ph.D. pathway. The early years emphasize statistical and computational research; later years shift toward data governance, privacy, AI policy, institutional strategy and public-policy implementation.

horizons.question: What can I enter now?
horizons.output: Develop strong capability in statistics, machine learning, computational social science, causal inference, data governance and policy analysis.

horizons.question: How should I specialise?
horizons.output: Own a policy domain such as AI governance, privacy, digital public infrastructure, algorithmic accountability or data regulation.

horizons.question: How should I evolve?
horizons.output: Lead multidisciplinary data-policy programs involving governments, regulators, technology firms, researchers and civil society.

horizons.question: How can I remain relevant?
horizons.output: Shape data and AI governance as technology evolves, combining technical understanding with law, economics, ethics and institutional strategy.

Career progression

blocks.label: Typical planning ranges are

blocks.text: Ph.D. routes

A senior Data Policy Advisor should remain technically credible while becoming increasingly capable of shaping institutional rules. Keep current with foundation models, synthetic data, privacy-enhancing technologies, algorithmic auditing, digital public infrastructure, data markets and AI regulation. The central skill is translating complex technical risks and opportunities into policies that are proportionate, enforceable and useful.
